etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French combiner, from Late Latin combīnāre (“unite, yoke together”), from Latin con- (“together”) + bīnī (“two by two”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To bring (two or more things or activities) together; to unite.

quote.citation: 2012 March, William E. Carter, Merri Sue Carter, “The British Longitude Act Reconsidered”, in American Scientist, volume 100, number 2, page 87:
quote.text: Conditions were horrendous aboard most British naval vessels at the time. Scurvy and other diseases ran rampant, killing more seamen each year than all other causes combined, including combat.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To have two or more things or properties that function together.

quote.citation: 1675, John Dryden, Aureng-zebe: A Tragedy. […], London:  […]  T[homas] N[ewcomb] for Henry Herringman, […], published 1676, →OCLC, (please specify the page number):
quote.text: You with your foes combine, / And seem your own destruction to design.

quote.citation: 1805, Walter Scott, “(please specify the page)”, in The Lay of the Last Minstrel: A Poem, London:  […]  [James Ballantyne] for Longman, Hurst, Rees, and Orme, […], and A[rchibald] Constable and Co., […], →OCLC:
quote.text: So sweet did harp and voice combine.

definitions.definition: (card games) In the game of casino, to play a card which will take two or more cards whose aggregate number of pips equals those of the card played.
(obsolete) To bind; to hold by a moral tie.

quote.citation: c. 1603–1604 (date written), William Shakespeare, “Measure for Measure”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act IV, scene iii]:
quote.text: I am combined by a sacred vow.

quote.citation: 1976, The Wurzels, I Am A Cider Drinker:
quote.text: When those combine wheels stops turnin'And the hard days work is doneTheres a pub around the cornerIt's the place we 'ave our fun

definitions.definition: Especially, a joint enterprise of whatever legal form for a purpose of business or in any way promoting the interests of the participants, sometimes with monopolistic or fraudulent intentions.
An industrial conglomeration in a socialist country, particularly in the former Soviet bloc.
(art) An artwork falling between painting and sculpture, having objects embedded into a painted surface.
(American football) A Test match in which applicants play in the hope of earning a position on a professional football team.

quote.citation: 2008, Scott Shetler, Optimal Performance Techniques for the Football Combine, page 5:
quote.text: If you purchased this book chances are that you are planning on participating in a football combine or pro-day test.

quote.citation: 2020, Jay R. Hoffman, The Science of American Football:
quote.text: In 2008, a study was published that examined the ability of the NFL combine to predict football playing performance in the NFL (Kuzmits and Adams, 2008).

quote.citation: 2020 April 24, Ken Belson, Ben Shpigel, “Full Round 1 2020 N.F.L. Picks and Analysis”, in New York Time‎[1]:
quote.text: At the combine, Reagor compared himself to the 49ers’ Deebo Samuel or Chiefs’ Tyreek Hill — whom he said he watched “every day”
